The writer and director of the movie has/ put so many efforts to bring the cinematic narrative/ to life, delivering a compelling experience for audience.
options_en: the writer and director of the movie has
to life, delivering a compelling experience for audience

questions.q_en:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

The proposed charter is intended to replace a constitution imposed by a military dictatorship 41 years ago.
questions.solution_en:
The verb 'intend' means 'to have as a plan or purpose'. We usually use 'to + infinitive' with the verb 'intend'. "We intend to go to Australia next year." So, the underlined part of the sentence is correct. Therefore, no improvement is required.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note:

Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

· To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

· My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

· To vote in elections is our right. [the infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

· Radha went to the lake to fetch water. [the infinitive 'to fetch', like a noun, is the object of the verb 'went', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (water)]

· The above sentences illustrate various ways in which infinitives are used. It can both act as a noun and a verb.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. From this chrysalis, a fully formed adult butterfly emerges, its wings initially crumpled and wet, needing time to expand and dry before it can take its first flight.

B. This remarkable journey begins when a female monarch lays her eggs exclusively on milkweed plants, which will serve as the sole food source for the forthcoming larvae.

C. After consuming enough milkweed to grow substantially, the caterpillar attaches itself upside down to a twig and transforms into a pupa, encased within a beautiful jade-green chrysalis.

D. The lifecycle of the monarch butterfly is a captivating example of complete metamorphosis, involving four distinct and visually stunning stages from its beginning to its end.
questions.solution_en:
The correct sequence is DBCA. Sentence D serves as an excellent introduction, presenting the overall topic - the "lifecycle of the monarch butterfly" and stating that it has four stages. Sentence B describes the very first step of "this remarkable journey," explaining where the eggs are laid, logically beginning the chronological sequence. Sentence C describes the next stage in the process, detailing what happens "after the caterpillar consumes enough milkweed" and when the caterpillar forms a chrysalis. Finally, sentence A describes the final stage of the metamorphosis, explaining how the adult butterfly emerges "From this chrysalis" (mentioned in C), completing the four-stage cycle.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Perhaps he helped turn their home into a saint arcade by requisitioning church overstock; but by any measure, it was quite a display.

B. There had to be six or seven larger-than-kid-sized statues on the second-floor landing, right at the top of the stairs.

C. Uncle John, now late in life, worked part-time as a janitor for our parish.

D. There they stood, in various poses of melancholy, misery, piety and/or penance, hands beckoning, in two-finger blessings with thumb and ring finger circled, or else holding something significant to each.

The correct sequence of the sentences will be:

A. Perhaps he helped turn their home into a saint arcade by requisitioning church overstock; but by any measure, it was quite a display.

B. There had to be six or seven larger-than-kid-sized statues on the second-floor landing, right at the top of the stairs.

D. There they stood, in various poses of melancholy, misery, piety and/or penance, hands beckoning, in two-finger blessings with thumb and ring finger circled, or else holding something significant to each.

Identifying the first sentence in the paragraph is a basic step to solve the para jumble. Among the given sentences, C can be easily identified as the introductory sentence as it introduces us to Uncle John, who is old and used to work part-time as a cleaner for the author's parish.

A is in continuation of C as it tells us more about Uncle John. It is mentioned that maybe he assisted in the transformation of their home into a saint arcade by obtaining church leftovers, but it was an impressive show in any case.

Thereafter, B carries forward the paragraph as it gives us the details of the figures or statues brought from the church by Uncle John. On the second floor, just at the top of the stairs, there had to be six or seven big sculptures.

D is the concluding sentence as it mentions the characteristics of the statues - already talked about in B.

Therefore, the correct answer is: (b) CABD.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The shareholders will elect him a director.
options_en: He will be elected as director by the shareholders.
The shareholders have elected him a director.
The shareholders elected him a director.
He will be elected a director.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the Future Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

The options except (1) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: "He will be elected as director by the shareholders.

questions.q_en:

After the fire, only the ________ walls of the old house remained.

Option a) bear is a noun (an animal) or a verb (to carry, to endure). As an adjective, it doesn't exist in a way that fits this context. "Bear walls" is not a standard English phrase describing a condition.

Option d) rare is an adjective, meaning uncommon or infrequently occurring. While walls can be rare, the context of a fire suggests a condition of being stripped or empty, not uncommonness.

So, a complete sentence is: After the fire, only the bare walls of the old house remained.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

The President said, "The market is going through a rough patch and we must invest accordingly."
options_en: The President said that the market has been going through a rough patch and they had to invest accordingly.
The President said that the market was going through a rough patch and they had to invest accordingly.
The President said that the market was going through a rough patch and they were to invest accordingly.
The President said that the market was going through a rough patch and they ought to invest accordingly.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is(b) The President said that the market was going through a rough patch and they had to invest accordingly.

Key points:

·The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Present Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech will be in Past Continuous Tense.

·Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object).

·For example:

o He said, "I am checking the assignment." (Direct Speech)

o He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

·If the use of "must" doesn't denote universality or morality, it changes to 'had to'.

·For example:

o Rahul said, "I must go to school at once."

o Rahul said that he had to go to school at once.

·The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

Direct SpeechIndirect Speech
saidsaid that
is goingwas going
wethey
musthad to

·Therefore, the correct answer is:The President said that the market was going through a rough patch and they had to invest accordingly.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The Swami asked the villagers to bring him a bottle of milk.
options_en: "Bring me a bottle of milk", the Swami told the villagers.
"Bring him a bottle of milk", the Swami told the villagers.
"Bring me a bottle of milk", the Swami commands the villagers.
"Bring mine a bottle of milk", the Swami tells the villagers.
questions.solution_en:
When the reporting verb of the reported speech is in simple past ('asked'), the reporting verb in the direct speech will also be in the simple past tense. ('asked')

'Mine' is a possessive pronoun, which is incorrect in the context. Therefore, option (d) is eliminated.

'Him' in option (b) changes the meaning of the sentence.

The Swami is not necessarily commanding the villagers to bring him a bottle of milk, but rather asking them.

The correct form of sentence in direct speech is: "Bring me a bottle of milk", the Swami told the villagers.

Therefore, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.

She saw a movie with her friends. She liked the _______ of the story.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank is 'source'. This word means the origin or basis of something. Filling the blank with 'source' implies that the subject 'she' liked the origins of the movie. Other options do not fit the blank contextually. 'Soar' means to fly or rise high in the air, 'sore' means painful or inflamed, and 'sauce' means a liquid or semi-liquid substance that adds flavour to food.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Employers in many developing countries report that a lack of skilled workers is a major and increasing bottleneck for their operations, affected their capacity to innovate.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence is: "Employers in many developing countries report that a lack of skilled workers is a major and increasing bottleneck for their operations, affected their capacity to innovate." The underlined segment is "affected their capacity," and we need the correct form.

· The sentence describes how the lack of workers impacts innovation capacity. The underlined part should be a participle modifying "operations" or a verb consistent with the clause.

· "Affect" (verb) means to influence; "effect" (noun) means result, or (verb) to bring about.

· Option A ("affect their capacity"): Present tense "affect" doesn't match the participle form needed to parallel "increasing bottleneck."

· Option B ("effecting their capacity"): "Effecting" means causing something to happen, which is incorrect here; we need "influencing."

· Option C ("effect their capacity"): "Effect" as a verb is wrong, and it doesn't fit grammatically.

· Option D ("affecting their capacity"): The gerund/participle "affecting" correctly describes the ongoing impact on capacity, parallel to "increasing" (e.g., "a bottleneck.. affecting their capacity").

The corrected sentence is: ".. a major and increasing bottleneck for their operations, affecting their capacity to innovate." Thus, Option D is correct.

One should measure one's _____ before buying the pants.
questions.solution_en:
Waist - This is the correct choice. The waist is the part of the body between the ribs and the hips. When buying pants, it is crucial to measure the waist to ensure a proper fit. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The final sentence: One should measure one's waist before buying the pants.

Vest - A vest is a sleeveless garment that is worn over a shirt. It is not a body part and is not relevant to the context of measuring for pants.

West - The direction towards the point of the horizon where the sun sets, and it has no connection to the human body or the act of buying pants.

Waste - It refers to material that is discarded or no longer needed. It is not relevant to the context of measuring for pants.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

I remember my mother taking me to the stadium.
options_en: I was taken to the stadium by mother that I remembered.
My mother remembered me taken to the stadium.
I remember being taken to the stadium by my mother.
I was remembered being taken to the stadium by my mother.
questions.solution_en:
To convert the active voice sentence "I remember my mother taking me to the stadium" to passive voice, we focus on the verb phrase "taking me to the stadium." In passive voice:

The object "me" becomes the subject.

The verb "taking" (present participle) changes to "being taken" (passive form).

The subject "my mother" becomes the agent, introduced by "by."

The verb "remember" remains unchanged, as it is not the verb being converted to passive. The structure becomes: "I remember being taken to the stadium by my mother."

Checking the options:

Option 1: "I was taken to the stadium by mother that I remembered" is grammatically incorrect and changes the meaning.

Option 2: "My mother remembered me taken to the stadium" incorrectly shifts the subject and is awkward.

Option 3: "I remember being taken to the stadium by my mother" is correct, maintaining the original meaning in passive voice.

Option 4: "I was remembered being taken to the stadium by my mother" incorrectly applies passive to "remember."

Thus, option 3 is the correct choice.

questions.q_en: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options_en: They have know each other since childhood.
Arnav has lived in this city for ten years.
We have just move into our new house.
They had buy tickets for the concert, but it was cancelled at the last minute.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence given in option (b) is grammatically correct.

Option (a) is not correct. In the present perfect tense (indicated by the helping verb 'have'), the correct form of the main verb after "have" is the past participle form. But 'know' (base form) is not the past participle form of the verb. Accordingly, 'know' should be replaced with the past participle form 'known'. The correct sentence is: They have known each other since childhood.

Option (c) is incorrect. In the present perfect tense (indicated by the helping verb 'have'), the correct form of the main verb after "have" is the past participle form. But 'move' (base form) is not the past participle form of the verb. Accordingly, 'move' should be replaced with the past participle form 'moved'. The correct sentence is: We have just moved into our new house.

Option (d) is also incorrect. In the past perfect tense (indicated by the helping verb 'had'), the correct form of the main verb after "had" is the past participle form. But the verb "buy" (base form) is not the past participle form of the verb. Accordingly, 'buy' should be replaced with the past participle form 'bought'. Also, "had bought" is used to indicate an action that occurred before another action in the past (in this case, the cancellation of the concert).

The correct sentence is: They had bought tickets for the concert, but it was cancelled at the last minute. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.
